summary: Columbia County, OR station with a warden's cabin, set up in 1913 per state forester reports; listed as removed; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed; no source gives a date or describes what, if anything, remains

Lookout reported most of its territory visible on almost every day of the 1914 season, per the state forester's later report

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The firelookout.com page with a cabin built in the 1920s and gone by the 1950s describes a different Rocky Point in Lincoln County. It is not used for this Columbia County record, and its dates do not replace the 1913 station.

notes_for_editor: Two WebSearch calls and about six page reads. The brief's second source page (firelookout.com/or/rockypoint.html) is the Lincoln County Rocky Point, 12 miles east of Lincoln City at 2,890 feet, a different lookout. It should come off this record's source_pages, and the Lincoln site should be checked as its own record. The Columbia County history rests on one page (Forest Lookouts), which quotes state forester reports for 1913 and 1914; its Removed tag has no date. The Forest Lookouts rocky-point1 page (an April 1913 Santiam River telephone item and a 1916 two-story cabin) appears to belong to Rocky (North) Point in Linn County, so it is not used. The brief's coordinates (45.82483, -123.2954) could not be checked against any source. The sources describe a warden's cabin and a station, not a tower, so the kind field is left as the record has it. No height or access facts were found. Fact-check 2026-10-10: source 2 stays listed because the story cites it only to separate the Lincoln County site from this record. The telephone sentence now states the report's stated purpose instead of its effect.
